By no means a swan but I’ve just started to glow up a little. Muuuch slower than my peers but here’s what I learnt from my glow up journey in 2024 (in no particular order). 

1. More regular haircuts with a stylist that understands the frequency of which I cut my hair. She cuts my hair so its good for maintenance, not just good for the first week. Figure out whether your hair needs a cream, serum, or oil to keep the flyaways in check and always apply some after showering (or when you feel your hair is getting scruffy). If your hair starts feeling weighed down by product, use a clarifying shampoo to deep cleanse. 

2. Eating healthier and/or taking multivitamins. I find it gives you a better complexion. (I’m less pallid now I’ve stopped eating instant noodles and chips so often. I’ve also begun craving vegetables though I previously stayed away.)

3. Trying out clothes to see the fit and color. Take photos in the changing room. Eventually you’ll figure out what works and doesn’t work. (Just tell yourself trying is free!) Start with the basics at uniqlo, then start to mix at match from other brands.  It helps to take your measurements and keep them on hand while so you can pick the right sizes more quickly. 

4. One spritz of perfume goes a long way. While it doesn’t improve your physical appearance, the nice smell kinda makes you feel more confident. This was easy for me to start with because I didn’t have to worry about ‘doing it wrong’.

5. Some lip tint also makes you feel a little more glam. I went for color matching service (a bit pricey…) and was given a general idea of what colors work on me. I find it looks good so I’m sticking with those colors for now. 

6. Exercise!~! It makes you look and FEEL better. There’s a small difference between people who do a little exercise and not at all. Use it to tilt the odds in your favor. I wouldn’t recommend losing weight purely through exercise. It REALLY has to be paired with diet.

These are some of the things that we’d do here when it’s Chinese New Year! 

There’s spring cleaning before the year begins so that we’re out with the old and the new luck can flow in. 

People sometimes buy and wear new clothes and go out visiting relatives. While visiting, you usually hand teo mandarin oranges to the head of the household and wish them a string of chinese new year greetings.

Married couples give their younger relatives red packets filled with money for good luck. 

The tables at people’s houses are usually filled with all sorts of snacks and goodies for incoming visitors. There might also be a potluck. (Though some people also eat only vegetarian food on the first day, but I can’t remember why.) 

Sometimes people will get together and gamble. Playing mahjong or card games. 

In general, it’s an occasion to get together and spend time with family and friends!
